task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict winning?
What sample size and exposure is needed to test mix adherence against series outcomes?
How should the recommended mix be derived without outcome leakage?
What confounders and label errors threaten an adherence-outcome test?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval call returned no records, so no earlier study by this project on this question is available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether adherence to a suppression-conditional mix predicts winning.
Whether the recommended mix was derived in a way that avoids outcome leakage.
Any effect size, variance, or power estimate for this question.
own_inferences: The outcome is binary at the series level, and the stated 54 series is a small number of units for detecting a modest adherence effect.
Adherence is probably correlated with team quality, injuries, and coaching, which are confounders the 54-series sample cannot adjust for well.
The 2025-26 playoffs are incomplete as of 2026-06-16 (complete only from 2026-06-21), so any series from that season must be excluded or treated as censored.
If the recommended mix is fit on the same play-by-play and matchup data used to score outcomes, adherence and winning share a derived label, so the association could be circular.
uncertainties: The count of 54 series does not obviously match the full set of playoff series across the stated seasons, so the exact unit inventory needs checking.
The mapping from a per-series mix to the defensive matchup and play-type records has not been specified.
The definition of 'suppression-conditional' and the adherence metric are not given in the task.
Whether any prior work exists outside this project's records is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned no records, so no prior finding, failed approach, or prior work changed the assessment. The decision rests on the design constraints of the stated data: 54 series units, a partially complete 2025-26 playoff season, and an adherence metric that may be derived from the outcome data.

blocking_constraints.text: With about 54 binary series outcomes, power to detect a moderate adherence effect is low, so a null result would be uninformative.
If the recommended mix is derived from the same play-by-play outcomes, adherence is not independent of the label.
Mix recommendations and adherence must be computed only from information available before each series starts; in-series play-by-play would leak the outcome.
Team strength, injuries, and coaching decisions may drive both adherence and winning, and 54 series cannot adjust for them.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so the question's prior status cannot be determined from [prior work] available.

risks.text: 54 series units give low power for a binary outcome; a null result cannot be read as evidence of no effect.
A recommended mix derived from outcome-linked play-by-play can make adherence a proxy for winning.
In-series or post-series data used to build the mix or measure adherence would inflate the association.
Team quality, injuries, and matchup mismatches are unmeasured or only partly measured confounders of adherence and winning.
Defensive and offensive schemes change across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so a mix that suppresses in one season may not transfer to another.
Some play types and lineups occur rarely within a series, so per-series adherence estimates are noisy.
Adherence measured from partial possessions and defensive matchup minutes may have low reliability at series level.
Searching over many mix definitions, thresholds, and seasons would inflate false positives.
Playoff series outcomes are close to balanced, so the base rate gives little leverage without a strong adherence signal.

design.estimand: Association between a pre-specified, outcome-blind adherence score to a suppression-conditional mix and series win probability, adjusted for team strength measured before each series.
design.unit: Playoff series (one row per series, with the adherence score computed for each team within the series).
design.sample: All complete playoff series from 2022-23 through 2024-25, plus 2025-26 series only after that playoff is complete (after 2026-06-21). Confirm the 54-series count against the full set of series before analysis.
design.power: Compute power before running, given 54 binary outcomes. If the minimum detectable effect is too large to be meaningful, treat the study as underpowered and report that rather than a null.
design.controls: Adjust for pre-series team rating or net rating, injuries and availability, home-court advantage, and seed or series round. Derive the recommended mix from data strictly before each series (rolling or out-of-sample), with no in-series or post-series information.
design.falsification: Use a placebo adherence score built from a mix recommended for a different suppression condition or a shuffled mix, and check that it shows no association with winning.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register a single primary adherence metric and a single model; treat any alternative metrics, thresholds, or seasons as exploratory with correction for multiple comparisons.
design.decision_rule: Support the hypothesis only if the primary adjusted association is positive with a confidence interval excluding zero and the placebo shows no association. Report a null only if power is adequate for a pre-stated minimum effect; otherwise report the result as inconclusive.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and derived play-type graph records for 2022-23 to 2025-26, frozen at a stated extraction date, with the 2025-26 playoffs excluded until complete (after 2026-06-21).
